scope: Actual combined owner/lease HandleTable and stable RangeClaim references. Read-only source review; no execution or inherited qualification.

data_structure.record_types: Allocation and Lease are the actual plain scalar/pointer records instantiated by HandleTable<Record>; compile-time trivially-copyable constraint is present.
data_structure.table_policy: One inline record; power-of-two fallback with at most 3/4 occupancy, linear probing and backshift deletion; all modes share the same implementation.
data_structure.identity: IDs are still taken under domain mutex, nonzero, strictly increasing and not recycled. Moving private Slot values does not change public identity.
data_structure.copy_move: Deleted copy construction/assignment suppress implicit move. The domain is also nonmovable through its mutex.
data_structure.growth: Fresh array allocation and scalar record rehash complete before swapping ownership. On fresh allocation failure, all old records and locations remain intact. The concrete Record copies and post-swap insertion are nonthrowing.

reference_audit.conclusion: insert_fresh returns Allocation&, committed immediately while locked. No callback, unlock or later owner-table mutation occurs before this reference is finished; Backing is an independent stable list element.

The pending record is inserted before releasing the domain lock. No Slot/Allocation reference is carried through unlock at 663. The function retains only id and stable backing_it, then reacquires the current Allocation with find(id) at 687. Other owner insertion, growth or backshift while the callback runs is safe.

The external pending record is inserted before unlock at 773. Success publication uses a fresh find(id) after relock, not a pre-callback address. Input descriptor is copied and Backing remains in the list.

A pending placeholder has owner=false/pending=true. Normal owner release and borrow reject it. pending and nonempty records prevent quiet reset/trim/collect/destroy from deleting it while its callback is in flight.

The held Allocation& belongs to the owner table. insert_fresh mutates only the distinct lease table; it cannot move this owner record. Permission/count checks precede insertion, reader/writer and out publication follow it. OOM publishes no lease and changes no reader/writer count.

All Allocation fields and Backing* are consumed before allocations.erase_found(found). No owner Slot/reference is dereferenced afterward. The following standalone callback uses only the captured stable Backing pointer/detached list.

Lease allocation ID/writer are read before leases.erase_found(record); record is never used afterward. The owner Slot remains valid because that erase mutates the other table. If retiring owner finishes, bytes and Backing* are read before owner erase, and neither owner pointer/reference is used afterward.

Backing is moved by std::list::splice into a detached list, which preserves its element address. Neither table location is held. Other threads may mutate both handle tables while unlocked without invalidating the detached Backing; pending keeps domain/provider lifetime admitted.

Both table release_storage calls are behind caller quiet checks, so no active/pending/retiring metadata is discarded. maintenance and pending are set before unlock, preventing new allocation or premature cleanup. Detached Backing elements and claims are independent of table storage.

owner_lifetime_proofs: An owner record remains present while owner=true or any reader/writer survives. Lease records keep an allocation ID scalar, not an Allocation pointer, so any owner-table movement is resolved by the next lookup.
A pending owner record cannot be legitimately erased while its callback is in flight. Re-find after callback is therefore expected to exist even if its physical Slot changed.

Shared Arena Backing is not individually reclaimed when a suballocation record ends; owned Arena chunks are reclaimed only at quiet bulk cleanup. SYSTEM and external Backings each have the original standalone ownership path.
Backing* inside Allocation targets std::list storage, not either moving HandleTable. List insertion and splicing of other nodes do not invalidate that element.
Default domain snapshot active_allocations/active_leases continues to use logical table size, including pending/retiring owner records exactly as before.
claim_cleanup_audit: Each successful claim reserve/import inserts one list element before setting claim_node and then claim_active=true. Initial inactive references are not dereferenced.

std::list RangeClaim iterators remain valid across insertion/removal of other registry nodes. The registry mutex still protects the overlap scan, releasing marker and erasure; lock order remains domain -> registry, with callbacks outside both locks.

publish_owned_claim still scans all other non-releasing claims for overlap, now excluding its own node by iterator identity. claim_range still enforces external ID uniqueness and overlap. The token counter and overflow behavior remain present.
Normal cleanup has one explicit mutable Backing owner. drop_claim checks active, erases exactly its node, and then clears active/iterator. Backing destruction does not implicitly drop a claim.

Rollback copies Backing into a local failed value, then erases the original owner record and original Backing before unlocking. The local copy becomes the sole cleanup path; destruction of the removed original does not perform a second drop.
Normal standalone cleanup splices the actual Backing element, and bulk cleanup iterates mutable detached Backings; each successful drop clears that same owner instance.

Unsafe provider alias and unknown retain/release outcomes do not drop the uncertain claim. Reservation/backing charge and poisoned-domain isolation remain, with no callback retry. A registry node can intentionally outlive the temporary iterator owner; it stores range/id data, not a domain pointer. This is isolation, not leak freedom.
memory_and_failure_limits: Generic owner and lease fallback arrays can retain high-water capacity while any corresponding record remains. Owner records include pending and retiring states, so owner=false does not itself mean metadata is empty.

After growth succeeds, a later claim/provider admission failure may erase the new record yet leave larger capacity while other records survive. Logical publication/budget rollback is preserved, but exact metadata footprint need not revert to its pre-call size.
Each table returns its fallback when its last record is erased; quiet trim/collect also release both storages. No array is retained across an empty table.

During doubling, old C and fresh 2C arrays coexist. Owner Slots are larger than lease Slots; combined peak requested metadata can rise even where stable storage or allocator call count falls. Measure actual requests and peaks separately.

Backing and RangeClaim definitions exactly match f9882d8, but the expected Release Backing sizeof of 80 bytes is not certified by source comparison alone. Platform/build/STL sizes require the owning layout probe.
Average O(1) probing is not an adversarial worst-case bound. Metadata remains outside the existing backing budget; no RSS/OS allocation/energy saving is established here.
